state_normalisation.name: Qubit State Normalisation
state_normalisation.history: The amplitude postulates were stated by von Neumann (1932) for quantum mechanics in general. The qubit, a two-level system carrying one of these states, became the unit of quantum information in the 1990s.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.

bloch_vector_x.name: Bloch Vector, x Component
bloch_vector_x.history: Bloch (1946) introduced the sphere to describe the magnetisation of spin-1/2 nuclei. Quantum computing adopted it as the standard picture of a single qubit.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Bloch, F. (1946). Nuclear induction. Physical Review, 70(7-8), 460-474.

bloch_vector_y.name: Bloch Vector, y Component
bloch_vector_y.history: The Bloch sphere picture was introduced for nuclear magnetic resonance by Bloch (1946). Its use for single qubits followed in the quantum information literature.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Bloch, F. (1946). Nuclear induction. Physical Review, 70(7-8), 460-474.

bloch_vector_z.name: Bloch Vector, z Component
bloch_vector_z.history: Bloch (1946) introduced the sphere for nuclear spins. The z axis is the standard computational basis direction in quantum computing.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Bloch, F. (1946). Nuclear induction. Physical Review, 70(7-8), 460-474.

born_rule_hadamard_plus.name: Born Rule (Hadamard on |0>)
born_rule_hadamard_plus.history: Born (1926) proposed that squared amplitudes give measurement probabilities. This is the measurement postulate that quantum algorithms rely on at their output.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Born, M. (1926). Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge. Zeitschrift für Physik, 37, 863-867.

hadamard_unitary.name: Hadamard Gate Is Unitary
hadamard_unitary.history: The matrix is named after Hadamard, whose matrices of this form appeared in the 1890s. Its role as a single-qubit gate was standardised in quantum circuit notation during the 1990s.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.

pauli_squares.name: Pauli Matrices Square to Identity
pauli_squares.history: Pauli (1927) introduced the matrices to describe the spin of the electron. Their algebra underlies the Pauli gates of quantum computing.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Pauli, W. (1927). Zur Quantenmechanik des magnetischen Elektrons. Zeitschrift für Physik, 43, 601-623.

pauli_product.name: Pauli Product Rule
pauli_product.history: Pauli (1927) gave the algebra of the spin matrices. The cyclic relation XY = iZ is the basic identity behind their use as quantum gates.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Pauli, W. (1927). Zur Quantenmechanik des magnetischen Elektrons. Zeitschrift für Physik, 43, 601-623.

rotation_z_unitary.name: Z-Rotation Gate Is Unitary
rotation_z_unitary.history: The rotation is the exponential of a Pauli matrix, so its unitarity follows from the Pauli algebra. Parameterised rotations became standard single-qubit gates in quantum circuit design.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.

bell_state_from_hadamard_and_cnot.name: Bell State from Hadamard and CNOT
bell_state_from_hadamard_and_cnot.history: Bell (1964) showed that entangled states give correlations no local hidden-variable theory can reproduce. The Hadamard-then-CNOT circuit is the standard way to prepare one of these states.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Bell, J. S. (1964). On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen paradox. Physics, 1(3), 195-200.

grover_two_qubits_one_iteration.name: Grover Search, Two Qubits, One Iteration
grover_two_qubits_one_iteration.history: Grover (1996) gave a quadratic speedup for unstructured search. For four items the speedup is exact after a single iteration, the case used as the textbook example.
citations: Grover, L. K. (1996). A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search. Proceedings of the 28th ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC), 212-219.
Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.

shor_factor_from_order.name: Shor Factoring from Order (N = 15)
shor_factor_from_order.history: Shor (1997) showed that finding the period of modular exponentiation is solvable in polynomial time on a quantum computer. Factoring then reduces to classical number theory.
citations: Shor, P. W. (1997). Polynomial-time algorithms for prime factorization and discrete logarithms on a quantum computer. SIAM Journal on Computing, 26(5), 1484-1509.
Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.

qft_unitary_n4.name: Quantum Fourier Transform Is Unitary (N = 4)
qft_unitary_n4.history: The discrete Fourier transform is classical. Coppersmith (1994) gave an approximate version that fits quantum circuits, and Shor (1997) used the transform to find periods.
citations: Nielsen, M. A., & Chuang, I. L. (2010). Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Shor, P. W. (1997). Polynomial-time algorithms for prime factorization and discrete logarithms on a quantum computer. SIAM Journal on Computing, 26(5), 1484-1509.
